questions.enonce_markdown:
A car moves at a constant velocity on a straight road.

(i) Define acceleration and give its unit. *[3 marks]*

(ii) What is the net force acting on the car? Explain your answer. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Acceleration** is the **rate of change of velocity**, that is the change in velocity per unit time: $a = \dfrac{v-u}{t}$. Its unit is the **metre per second squared** ($\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$).

(ii) The net (resultant) force on the car is **zero**.

**Explanation:** a constant velocity (same speed, same direction) means the acceleration is zero. By Newton's laws ($F = ma$, with $a = 0$) the resultant force must be zero: the forward driving force of the engine is **balanced** by the backward resistive forces (friction and air resistance), and the weight is balanced by the reaction of the road.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A stone is thrown vertically upwards with an initial velocity of $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ at a place where the acceleration due to gravity is $10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$.

(i) Calculate the time taken by the stone to reach the maximum height. *[3 marks]*

(ii) Calculate the maximum height attained by the stone. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Take upward as positive: $u = 20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $a = -g = -10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$. At the maximum height the velocity is $v = 0$.

(i) $v = u + at \Rightarrow 0 = 20 - 10\,t \Rightarrow$ **$t = 2\,\mathrm{s}$**.

(ii) $v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 20^2 - 2\times 10\times h \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{400}{20} = $ **$20\,\mathrm{m}$**.

Check: $h = ut - \tfrac{1}{2}gt^2 = 20\times 2 - 5\times 2^2 = 40 - 20 = 20\,\mathrm{m}$.

questions.enonce_markdown:
An object of mass $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ travelling with a velocity of $20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ collides with, and sticks to a stationary object of mass $3\,\mathrm{kg}$. They both move off together in the same direction with a new velocity.

(i) State the law of conservation of linear momentum. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Calculate the total momentum of the system just before collision. *[3 marks]*

(iii) Calculate the new velocity of the two objects moving together. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Law of conservation of linear momentum:** when bodies collide (or interact) in a system on which **no external resultant force acts**, the **total momentum before the collision is equal to the total momentum after** it, in the same direction.

(ii) Momentum $= mv$; the $3\,\mathrm{kg}$ object is at rest, so it has no momentum:

$$p_{\text{before}} = 2\times 20 + 3\times 0 = 40\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$$

(iii) The objects stick together, so the total mass is $2 + 3 = 5\,\mathrm{kg}$. By conservation of momentum:

$$40 = (2+3)\,v \Rightarrow v = \dfrac{40}{5} = 8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$$

The two objects move off together at **$8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$**, in the direction of motion of the $2\,\mathrm{kg}$ object.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State the basic law of magnetism. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Give the difference in the magnetic properties of soft-iron and steel. *[2 marks]*

(iii) Give one use each of soft-iron and steel in magnetism. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Basic law of magnetism:** **like poles repel and unlike poles attract**.

(ii) **Soft iron** is **easily magnetised and easily demagnetised**: it is a temporary magnet. **Steel** is **harder to magnetise but keeps its magnetism**: it is a permanent magnet.

(iii) **Soft iron:** the core of an electromagnet (also: transformer core, electric bell, relay). **Steel:** a permanent magnet (for example a compass needle, or the magnet of a loudspeaker or of a door catch).

questions.enonce_markdown:
Consider the N-pole and the S-pole of two bar magnets placed close to each other and a straight current-carrying conductor with current flowing into the page.

(i) Draw the magnetic field pattern of the current-carrying conductor and the magnetic field pattern between the poles. *[4 marks]*

(ii) Draw the combined magnetic field pattern when the current-carrying conductor is placed between the poles of the bar magnets. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(The drawings are to be made by the candidate; they are described here, with the N pole on the left and the S pole on the right.)*

(i) **Conductor alone:** a set of **concentric circles** centred on the wire, getting farther apart away from it. For a current **into the page** the field is **clockwise** (right-hand grip rule), shown by arrows on the circles.

**Between the poles alone:** **straight, parallel, equally spaced lines** running from the **N pole to the S pole** (left to right), with arrows pointing from N to S. The field is uniform in the middle and the lines bulge outwards a little near the edges of the poles.

(ii) **Combined pattern:** the wire is placed in the middle of the uniform field. The circular field of the wire **adds** to the magnet's field on the side where both point the same way (above the wire, where the clockwise circle points left to right): the lines are **crowded** there. It **opposes** the magnet's field below the wire: the lines are **spread out**, and at one point near the wire the two fields cancel (a **neutral point**). The lines are distorted around the wire, like a curve that bends away from the crowded side. The wire therefore feels a force **from the strong-field side to the weak-field side** (downwards here, by Fleming's left-hand rule). If the poles are interchanged, all the arrows and the direction of the force are reversed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
A transformer with 800 turns in the primary coil is operated by an a.c. input of $240\,V$. The output of this transformer is connected to a lamp rated $6\,V$, $24\,W$.

(i) State Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Calculate the number of turns in the secondary coil. *[3 marks]*

(iii) State one method by which energy is lost in a transformer and explain how it is minimized in this transformer. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Faraday's law:** the **magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is directly proportional to the rate of change of magnetic flux linkage** (the rate at which the conductor cuts the magnetic field lines).

(ii) The lamp is rated $6\,\mathrm{V}$, so the secondary voltage is $V_s = 6\,\mathrm{V}$ (the $24\,\mathrm{W}$ rating is not needed). For an ideal transformer $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$:

$$N_s = N_p\times\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = 800\times\dfrac{6}{240} = 20\ \text{turns}$$

The secondary coil has **20 turns** (a step-down transformer). (Check: the lamp current is $24/6 = 4\,\mathrm{A}$ and the primary current $24/240 = 0.1\,\mathrm{A}$.)

(iii) **Energy loss by eddy currents** in the iron core: the changing flux induces currents in the core, which heat it. This is **minimized by making the core of thin laminated sheets of soft iron, insulated from one another**, so that eddy currents are small. (Other acceptable answers: heating of the copper coils, $I^2R$, reduced by using thick copper wire of low resistance; flux leakage, reduced by winding both coils on the same closed core; hysteresis loss, reduced by using soft iron.)
